rollback_evidence: G64 (IOS-M028, IOS-M029), measured on IOSv 15.9(3)M12 (router, GNS3 d-iosv), task netops-20261119-590 (task-evidence/g64). The Admin snapshot carries the ACL listings (show ip access-lists, show ipv6 access-list) as comments because IOS 15.9 omits the rule sequence numbers in the running configuration; the configuration block must agree with the listing rule for rule. The safeguard is the revert timer of the interface profile. The key is ipv4:<name> or ipv6:<name> (a named extended ACL; standard, numbered and ACLs with remarks, log, port ranges or other options are outside the profile and refused). Rules are comma separated, explicitly sequenced permit or deny entries for ip/ipv6, tcp, udp or icmp: 'SEQ permit|deny PROTOCOL SOURCE DESTINATION [eq PORT]' with any, host ADDRESS or a network in prefix form (IPv4 is written to the device with a wildcard mask); TCP and UDP accept one destination eq port. IPv4 lines: 'ip access-list extended NAME', 'SEQ permit|deny ...', 'no SEQ'; IPv6 lines: 'ipv6 access-list NAME', 'sequence SEQ permit|deny ...' ('SEQ permit' is refused by the IPv6 ACL mode), 'no sequence SEQ'. Update sends only the rules that change (undo restores the exact sequence numbers and order); an ACL attached to an interface or used elsewhere (VTY access-class, route-map, NAT, QoS) can only be updated to another nonempty rule list, with endpoint_impact naming the key when the attachment is on an up interface or the name is used elsewhere; an ACL on the management path must keep SSH permitted. The check account reads show ip access-lists NAME / show ipv6 access-list NAME (an empty IPv6 ACL and a missing one both list nothing; the write account's running configuration tells them apart).
